title: A Subtraction Nim with a Pass
summary: We consider a subtraction Nim with subtraction set {s_1,s_2,s_3={2,4n,4n+2}, where n is a positive integer such that n >= 3. We do not treat the case that n=1 or n=2 in this article. We show that this game satisfies the reverse-mex property of Grundy numbers, i.e., G(x)=mex{G(x+s_1), G(x+s_2), G(x+s_3)}, where the mex is taken over successors rather than predecessors. We modify the rule of this subtraction Nim to allow a one-time pass, that is, a passing move usable at most once during the game, unavailable from terminal positions; once used by either player, it becomes unavailable.
